title: Kishore Biyani v. State of U.P. & Anr.
disposition: Application allowed; summoning order, non-bailable warrant and complaint proceedings quashed
headnote: Not a Supply Code / electricity case. A Section 482 Cr.P.C. petition to quash a criminal complaint of breach of trust (IPC ss.406/405) against the former Executive Chairman of a retail chain over an unpaid food-supply bill; the Court held the transaction was a purely commercial sale (no 'entrustment' of property), the mandatory Section 202(1) Cr.P.C. enquiry (accused residing outside jurisdiction) was not held, and quashed the proceedings. No electricity supply or Supply Code issue is involved; flagged here only because the judgment surfaced in the source corpus.

holding_units.code: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Cr.P.C., 1973 (unrelated to the Electricity Act/Supply Code)
holding_units.topic: Criminal breach of trust — commercial sale is not 'entrustment'; mandatory Section 202(1) enquiry
holding_units.holding: A mere commercial sale transaction (unpaid supply of goods) does not amount to 'entrustment' of property under Section 405 IPC; absent entrustment and dishonest misappropriation, no offence under Section 406 is made out. Where the accused resides outside the trial court's jurisdiction, Section 202(1) Cr.P.C. mandates an enquiry before summoning, and its omission vitiates the summoning order.
holding_units.limiting_facts: No electricity/Supply Code facts; a food-products supplier's criminal complaint against the former Executive Chairman of 'Big Bazaar' (Future Retail Ltd.) over unpaid invoices, filed after the company entered NCLT insolvency/moratorium.
holding_units.flag: Entirely off-topic to the Supply Code jurisprudence; recorded only to keep the source-corpus review complete. No provision-holdings or authorities from this case are added to the Supply Code index.
